---
title: "Further Reading"
---

Short and annotated. The chapters cite everything they use; these are the sources most worth reading
in full.

## Classical RL

- Richard Sutton and Andrew Barto, *Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction*, 2nd ed.
  [@sutton2018reinforcement]. Chapter 2 (bandits, evaluative feedback), chapter 13 (policy gradients)
  and section 11.3 (the deadly triad) are the background this book assumes.
- John Schulman et al. on TRPO, GAE and PPO [@schulman2015trust; @schulman2015gae;
  @schulman2017proximal]: three short papers that define the policy-gradient machinery LLM training
  still uses. Schulman's note on approximating KL divergence [@schulman2020approximating] is two pages
  and explains $k_1$, $k_2$ and $k_3$.
- Sergey Levine, "Reinforcement Learning and Control as Probabilistic Inference"
  [@levine2018reinforcement], for the inference view behind the closed-form optimum.

## The RLHF lineage

- Christiano et al. [@christiano2017deep], Ziegler et al. [@ziegler2019finetuning], Stiennon et al.
  [@stiennon2020learning] and Ouyang et al. [@ouyang2022training], in that order: the recipe as it was
  built.
- Korbak, Perez and Buckley [@korbak2022rl]: why the KL penalty makes the objective a posterior.
- Gao, Schulman and Hilton [@gao2022scaling]: overoptimization measured.

## Beyond PPO

- Rafailov et al. [@rafailov2023direct] for DPO, and Azar et al. [@azar2023general] for the family it
  belongs to and its overfitting failure mode.
- Ahmadian et al. [@ahmadian2024back]: the case for simple REINFORCE-style estimators in RLHF.
- Shao et al. [@shao2024deepseekmath], section 5.2: the unified view of SFT, rejection sampling, DPO,
  PPO and GRPO by data source, reward and gradient coefficient, which this book's $(q, w)$ form follows.
- Liu et al. [@liu2025understanding] and Yu et al. [@yu2025dapo]: what GRPO's choices do, and what to
  change.

## What RL does to a model

- Yue et al. [@yue2025does] and Liu et al. [@liu2025prorl] read together, as the two sides of the
  pass@$k$ debate.
- Shenfeld, Pari and Agrawal [@shenfeld2025razor] on forgetting, and Kirk et al.
  [@kirk2023understanding] on generalization and diversity.

## This author's other books

- [loss-functions-lab](https://ioannisantoniadis.github.io/loss-functions-lab/): where Bradley–Terry,
  the DPO derivation and proper scoring rules are derived as losses.
- [modern-ai-systems-and-methods](https://ioannisantoniadis.github.io/modern-ai-systems-and-methods/):
  the short overview of RL, bandits and generative AI that this book expands.
- [transformer-atlas](https://github.com/ioannisantoniadis/transformer-atlas): the architectures, which
  this book treats as given.
